newsitem.title: USA: Post Office offers reward, but won't say for what.
newsitem.headline: Post Office offers reward, but won't say for what.

text.p: The U.S. Postal Service has offered a $25,000 reward for the return of several stolen items so secret that officials would only identify them as "devices."

Rafael Rivera, postal inspector for the Miami division, said one mail carrier was robbed three weeks ago, and two other carriers were robbed on Tuesday, according to a report in the Miami Herald on Friday.
The three victims surrendered what the robbers were after -- but Rivera said he couldn't be more specific than referring to the stolen goods as "devices."
"I can't say what their demands were," Rivera told the Herald. "I can't tell you what it is. I can't tell you what it's used for."
The devices were manufactured for the Postal Service and cannot be bought in stores, he said.
But the postal service is willing to give plenty of information about the description of the robbers, their stolen cars and license plate numbers, and the weapons they used.
A $25,000 reward is being offered for tips leading to the arrest and conviction of the robbers.
